title: Kalwings
notes: Welcome. In the next few minutes you will see how to run Kalwings as an admin, and how the code is organised for developers.

title: Five rules that never change
items: Never add a student or mentor who has not agreed to be listed.
Always shown on every listing. Unpaid roles say so.
Unless the student chooses to share it.
No made-up stats, logos, awards or testimonials.
No auto-rejection. Scores are advice. No guaranteed jobs.

steps.cap: Open the login page and type your email address.
Press Send one-time code. There are no passwords: a six-digit code is emailed to you.
Type the six-digit code from your inbox. It works for 10 minutes.
Press Log in. You land in your workspace.
Directory: companies, colleges, mentors and users live here.
Bulk upload: add many students, companies or mentors from a spreadsheet.
Launch readiness: a live checklist of what is still missing.
Add a company yourself: name, website, status and plan.
Search by name, or filter by status.
Open a company to manage it.
Edit details, upload a logo, set the career page address.
Verification: only verified companies can post and search.
Plan: choose which limits apply.
Team: add an HR person by name and email. They sign in with an emailed code.

title: 3. Post a listing for a company

steps.cap: Fill title, type, description, pay, mode, location, eligibility and deadline. Pay is mandatory.
Listings appear here. Close or reopen any time.
Add a college and verify it so students can pick it.
Edit a college whenever you need to.
Add a mentor with every detail: role, company, country, domain, topics and bio.
Edit later, or upload a photo for them. The mentor can update their own profile after signing in.
Add anyone: student, mentor, HR at another company, college admin or admin.
Change role: the account and all its data stay exactly as they were.
Role requests from users wait here. Approve or decline.
Search by name or email. Suspending is reversible and never deletes anyone.
In Settings, a user picks the role they need...
...explains why...
...and sends the request. Nothing changes until an admin approves.
Three panels: students, companies and mentors.
Each takes an Excel or CSV file, up to 1,000 rows.
Mentors need role, company, country and domain as well as name and email.
Download the template and keep its first row.
Choose your filled-in file.
Preview saves nothing. Every row shows ready, skipped or error.
Two ready, one error. Fix it or leave it out.
Import adds only the ready rows. One bad row never blocks the others.
Rename a plan.
Set the price text employers see.
Change the four limits: listings, challenges, assessments, team.
Save: every company on the plan sees it at once.
Press a plan button to switch a company. Its team is notified.
An announcement banner for every signed-in page.
The support email shown on Help and Contact.
Untick a role to close sign-ups for it.
Save. Changes show straight away.
If sign-in emails are not ticked, nobody can receive codes. Fix that first.
Real companies, colleges, mentors and listings: each line links to where you fix it.
Approve or reject new listings. Check pay, mode, location and eligibility are honest.
Every admin decision is recorded: who, what and when. Entries cannot be edited.

title: How a request flows
notes: A request flows from the browser to a server component, which checks the role and reads the database with Prisma.

title: Every server action follows six steps
steps: Who is calling? First line of every action.
Check and cap every input on the server.
Return friendly errors, do not throw.
Refresh pages and return a result.

title: Changing the database safely
steps: Generate the SQL from your local database.
New timestamped folder. Never edit an old one.
Compile the SQL into the build. Commit the generated file.
